Reasoning at test time

Module 22 · Using models well ← All explorables

A model can buy accuracy after training, by spending more tokens on each question: write out the steps (chain of thought), sample several answers and keep the most common (self-consistency), or have a grader pick one (best-of-n). Everything below is the module's real data: 200 GSM8K maths problems, each answered once greedily and 8 times at temperature 0.7 by Qwen3-1.7B with 4-bit weights, thinking mode off. Nothing here runs a model; the page reads cached replies.

1 · One problem, eight samples

Pick a problem. Slide n to vote over the first n samples. The best-of-n pick is the sample the model itself graded highest. Open a sample to read it.

2 · Accuracy as n grows

Each point averages over every way to choose n of the 8 samples, so no single lucky draw sets it. The page computes the curves from the cached answers. Hover a point for its value.

Accuracy against tokens the model wrote per problem, on a log scale. Best-of-n also makes the model read each sample once more to grade it; that reading is not counted here.
